title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction: This page continues the definition, begun at the bottom of p.21, of 'MD-courbes' (Mumford–Deligne curves), i.e. stable marked curves. Setting: S is a 'multiplicité schématique' (an algebraic stack), X → S is proper, flat and of finite presentation, and I ⊂ X is a closed subscheme, also flat and of finite presentation over S. The pair (X, I) is an MD-curve over S if every geometric fibre (X_s̄, I_s̄) is a geometric MD-curve. That means: X_s̄ is connected of dimension 1; its singular points do not lie in I_s̄ and are ordinary double points (nodes); and the infinitesimal rigidity (stability) condition holds. Grothendieck spells this condition out in two parts: X_s̄ is not a smooth genus-1 curve with I_s̄ = ∅, and every irreducible component of genus 0 has 'marked weight' ≥ 3. The marked weight is understood as marked points plus branches of nodes. In modern terms this is exactly the Deligne–Mumford–Knudsen stability condition, equivalent to finiteness of Aut(X_s̄, I_s̄), i.e. no infinitesimal automorphisms. He then contrasts this with §3 (moduli M_G of curves of fixed combinatorial type G, the 'dual graph' stratification). Here, even over a connected base such as a trait, the combinatorial type of the geometric fibres can jump from point to point. The numerical type (g, ν) cannot: g is fixed by the Euler characteristic χ(X_s, O_{X_s}), which is locally constant by flatness and properness, and ν = card I_s is locally constant by flatness/finiteness of I. So (g, ν) is a locally constant function on S, as completed on p.23. This prepares the statement on p.23 that the stack M̂_{g,ν} of MD-curves of type (g, ν) with 2g+ν ≥ 3 is representable by a smooth proper algebraic stack over Spec Z, the Deligne–Mumford–Knudsen compactification. It serves his programme of studying the 'structure at infinity' of M_{g,ν}, i.e. the boundary stratification and its relation to the Teichmüller tower and anabelian geometry.
errors: Minor gap: for I_s̄ to be a set of ν distinct marked points one needs I → S finite étale, equivalently I_s̄ reduced; this is not stated explicitly on this page, though it is presumably intended or implied by the earlier setup.

'Poids marqué' must count a self-node with multiplicity 2 (two branches) for the genus-0 condition to exclude the irreducible nodal rational curve with no marks. This is presumably intended but not stated.
Genus-1 components of a reducible curve need weight ≥ 1. This is automatic by connectedness, so the condition as stated is complete.

ideas.what: Definition of stable ν-pointed curves over a base (MD-curves): flat proper family, fibres connected nodal of dim 1, marked points disjoint from nodes, stability condition on genus 0 and genus 1 components
ideas.where_published: Mentioned in spirit in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), which discusses the Mumford–Deligne compactification and the 'structure at infinity' of the M_{g,ν}

ideas.what: Stability equals infinitesimal rigidity (finite automorphism group)
ideas.modern_name: Stability ⇔ Aut finite / no infinitesimal automorphisms

ideas.what: Combinatorial type (dual graph) varies in families, while the numerical type (g, ν) is locally constant via χ(O) and the degree of I
ideas.modern_name: Local constancy of arithmetic genus in flat proper families; boundary stratification by dual graphs
ideas.where_published: EGA III, local constancy of Euler characteristic in flat proper families

deep.surprise_reason: A careful but standard restatement of the Deligne–Mumford–Knudsen definition of stable pointed curves; the only personal touches are the terminology ('MD-courbe', 'poids marqué', 'multiplicité schématique'). Nothing new mathematically.
